features.name: cc_word_length_variance
features.definition: What is the variance of word length (in characters) across all words in the counter-argument comments?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments as a JSON list of strings; malformed/missing -> null; empty list -> null. Concatenate all comments, extract words with re.findall(r"[A-Za-z']+", text) (apostrophes kept, counted in length? no: strip apostrophes before measuring), compute each word's length in characters, and return the population variance (np.var, ddof=0) pooled over all words in all comments. If fewer than 2 words, return null. Raw text computation; no semantic filtering, so comments may contain outcome announcements.

h0: cc_word_length_variance has no association with delta.
h1: Higher cc_word_length_variance is associated with higher likelihood of delta (OP view change).
note: Persuasiveness operationalized as the delta outcome. Variance is pooled across all words in all counter-comments (the hypothesis does not specify per-comment vs pooled); variance of character length, population variance, with a simple regex tokenizer. Comments may include quotations, URLs, and outcome announcements; raw text is not outcome-free, and timing of replies is unknown. Association only, not causal. Comment count/length may affect variance; no controls added.
